<output>
Seqtk
-----

Seqtk is a fast and lightweight tool for processing sequences in the FASTA or
FASTQ format.

Usage Examples
--------------

* Convert FASTQ to FASTA:

        seqtk seq -a in.fq.gz > out.fa

* Convert ILLUMINA 1.3+ FASTQ to FASTA and mask bases with quality lower than 20 to lowercases (the 1st command line) or to `N` (the 2nd):

        seqtk seq -aQ64 -q20 in.fq > out.fa
        seqtk seq -aQ64 -q20 -n N in.fq > out.fa

* Fold long FASTA/Q lines and remove FASTA/Q comments:

        seqtk seq -Cl60 in.fa > out.fa

* Convert multi-line FASTQ to 4-line FASTQ:

        seqtk seq -l0 in.fq > out.fq

* Reverse complement FASTA/Q:

        seqtk seq -r in.fq > out.fq

* Extract sequences with names in file `name.lst`, one sequence name per line:

        seqtk subseq in.fq name.lst > out.fq

* Extract sequences in regions contained in file `reg.bed`:

        seqtk subseq in.fa reg.bed > out.fa

* Mask regions in `reg.bed` to lowercases:

        seqtk seq -M reg.bed in.fa > out.fa

* Subsample 10000 read pairs from two large paired FASTQ files (remember to use the same random seed to keep pairing):

        seqtk sample -s100 read1.fq 10000 > sub1.fq
        seqtk sample -s100 read2.fq 10000 > sub2.fq

* Trim low-quality bases from both ends using the Phred algorithm:

        seqtk trimfq in.fq > out.fq

* Trim 5bp from the left end of each read and 10bp from the right end:

        seqtk trimfq -b 5 -e 10 in.fa > out.fa

* Find telomere (TTAGGG)n repeats:

        seqtk telo seq.fa > telo.bed 2> telo.count
</output>

    proc = subprocess.Popen(['./executable'] + args, stdin=subprocess.PIPE,
                            stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
    out, err = proc.communicate(input=input_str.encode('utf-8'))
    return proc.returncode, out.decode('utf-8'), err.decode('utf-8')

fa = ">seq1 comment1\nACGTACGTACGT\n>seq2\nTGCA\n"
fq = "@seq1 comment1\nACGTACGTACGT\n+\nI!I!I!I!I!I!\n@seq2\nTGCA\n+\n!!!!\n"

print("--- Default FASTA ---")
rc, out, err = run_seqtk(['seq'], fa)
print(f"rc={rc}\nout:\n{out}err:\n{err}")

print("--- Default FASTQ ---")
rc, out, err = run_seqtk(['seq'], fq)
print(f"rc={rc}\nout:\n{out}err:\n{err}")

print("--- FASTA with -A ---")
rc, out, err = run_seqtk(['seq', '-A'], fq)
print(f"rc={rc}\nout:\n{out}err:\n{err}")

print("--- Line width -l 5 ---")
rc, out, err = run_seqtk(['seq', '-l', '5'], fa)
print(f"rc={rc}\nout:\n{out}err:\n{err}")

print("--- Drop comment -C ---")
rc, out, err = run_seqtk(['seq', '-C'], fa)
print(f"rc={rc}\nout:\n{out}err:\n{err}")

print("--- Reverse complement -r ---")
rc, out, err = run_seqtk(['seq', '-r'], fa)
print(f"rc={rc}\nout:\n{out}err:\n{err}")

print("--- Reverse complement FASTQ -r ---")
rc, out, err = run_seqtk(['seq', '-r'], fq)
print(f"rc={rc}\nout:\n{out}err:\n{err}")

EOF
python3 test_seq.py
"}

import subprocess
import os

def test_cmd(cmd_args, input_data="", files={}):
    for fname, fcontent in files.items():
        with open(fname, "w") as f:
            f.write(fcontent)
            
    p1 = subprocess.Popen(['./executable'] + cmd_args, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
    o1, e1 = p1.communicate(input_data.encode() if isinstance(input_data, str) else input_data)
    
    p2 = subprocess.Popen(['./my_executable'] + cmd_args, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
    o2, e2 = p2.communicate(input_data.encode() if isinstance(input_data, str) else input_data)
    
    rc1, rc2 = p1.returncode, p2.returncode
    out1, out2 = o1.decode(errors='replace'), o2.decode(errors='replace')
    err1, err2 = e1.decode(errors='replace'), e2.decode(errors='replace')
    
    ok = (rc1 == rc2) and (out1 == out2) and (err1 == err2)
    if not ok:
        print(f"FAIL: {cmd_args}")
        if rc1 != rc2: print(f"  RC diff: orig={rc1} my={rc2}")
        if out1 != out2: print(f"  OUT diff:\nORIG:\n{out1}\nMY:\n{out2}")
        if err1 != err2: print(f"  ERR diff:\nORIG:\n{err1}\nMY:\n{err2}")
    else:
        print(f"PASS: {cmd_args}")
    return ok
